parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the C++ migration task, Rust 2021/std-only constraints, Cargo plus standalone entry requirement, exact CLI/output matching, and black-box probing requirement.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent performed initial probing, then used a two-child swarm with agent-0 owning implementation and agent-1 owning differential verification; the parent owned the coordination loop and final closure.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 first created Cargo.toml, src modules, and test11.rs from the parent-provided behavioral spec, then rewrote the implementation to use byte slices, args_os, raw stdout writes, and length-limited validation after verifier feedback.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Implementation happened in the shared /output project but with a single writer; the final artifact tree included Cargo.toml, test11.rs, src modules, Cargo.lock, and release build outputs.
parallel.verification: The run built through cargo and rustc, compared outputs against the C++ binary, incorporated the verifier's mismatch report, and then reran a 576-case differential suite plus a parent quick sanity check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The first parallel implementation missed byte-length validation and raw argv robustness, but those gaps were corrected before closure; the official completed evaluation passed 40/40.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Rust migration requirements, exact byte-for-byte behavior, std-only implementation, CLI defaults, and black-box inference from the compiled C++ executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final reporting, so there was no delegation or handoff boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial actor implemented modules under an idna directory and a test11.rs entry point, including exact prefix handling, ASCII-only lowercasing, length-limited validity checks, ASCII/IDN checks, and label counting.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor wrote the Cargo project and standalone entry, compiled with rustc and cargo, and left an artifact tree containing test11.rs, Cargo files, idna modules, and release outputs.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran byte-for-byte comparisons against the C++ binary over documented examples, edge cases, length boundaries, control characters, multi-arg and no-arg cases, then the official evaluator passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official-evaluator failure remained; the serial final report still described std::env::args rather than the parallel run's later raw-argv hardening, but that did not prevent official 40/40 success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel tracked the Rust 2021, std-only, /output Cargo project, standalone test11.rs, exact output, and black-box probing obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and tracked the same user-visible migration obligations and example outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement coverage ended equivalent for official evaluation; parallel added raw-byte robustness after verifier feedback, while serial relied on local probing and still passed official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into an implementation child and a differential-verification child, with the parent orchestrating feedback and final acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, coding, building, and verification in one actor with no child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced coordination boundaries but also an independent verifier; serial avoided handoffs and solved linearly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The initial implementation brief contained a simplified spec, but the verifier returned concrete counterexamples and the parent forwarded exact corrective requirements to the implementer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor held its own probes and implementation decisions in one context, discovering the length limits before coding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an extra context transfer, yet the relevant verifier findings were not lost and were used; serial had no transfer risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Agent-0 changed the implementation from string-based functions to byte-slice functions and raw output after the verifier identified length and non-UTF-8 gaps.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented the length limits, ASCII-only lowercasing, prefix stripping, validation, and label-count behavior directly during the first solution path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached the final behavior through a fix cycle; serial reached official-passing behavior through its own local probing before final verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received the initial swarm result, acted on the verifier's failure report, resumed the implementation child, and then resumed the verifier for a full rerun.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local command results directly informed subsequent edits and the final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more lifecycle steps but no completed child result was stranded; serial had none to join.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the implementation child wrote source files, while the verifier read and executed the built binary; the parent later inspected the resulting tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote and built its own project tree without concurrent workspace access.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared workspace but with single-writer ownership, so no concrete write collision or provenance loss occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed child implementation checks, independent verifier checks, a post-fix full 576-case verifier rerun, parent sanity check, and official 40/40 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed byte-for-byte local comparisons across examples, boundaries, controls, and no-arg cases, then official 40/40 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader and independently owned after the initial mismatch; both produced sufficient official acceptance evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time and tokens because of two children and a fix cycle, but finished within budget and with the corrected solution.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with no child overhead and an official-passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget profile differed substantially, but neither run timed out or closed with unfinished required work.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show no discordance: both parallel and serial passed all 40 testcases. Parallel differed by using an implementer/verifier split and a corrective feedback cycle after the verifier found two early behavioral gaps. Serial solved in one trajectory after local probing. The parallel process consumed the verifier result and corrected the artifact before final delivery, so the observed coordination overhead did not produce an official outcome deficit.
parallel_contributors: Two-child split gave independent verification that caught length-limit and raw-argv issues before closure.
Parent resumed the implementation and verifier children with concrete findings and required a post-fix full corpus rerun.
serial_contributors: Single actor retained probing context and implemented the byte-length validity rules before final build.
Local byte-for-byte checks and official evaluation both passed without delegation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel first produced a string-based implementation with missing length/raw-byte behavior, then fixed it.
Serial final report described std::env::args and did not evidence the same raw-argv hardening, but this was not an official failing case.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; comparative strategy contrast only

candidates.reason: Implementation was explicitly assigned to agent-0, which wrote the project and later applied the required fixes.
There were not separately owned incompatible implementation components; agent-0 owned the source tree and parent coordinated verification.
The implementer created the required Cargo project and test11.rs entry, and the final artifact contained the expected assembled files.
The parent managed implementation, verification, corrective handoff, re-verification, final sanity check, and closure.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked productive work with a concrete deadline consequence; the implementation and verifier completed.
The parent did initial probing before spawning, but later parallel implementation and verification were productive and left no unfinished or insufficiently verified work.
No indispensable implementation or verification path was starved; both child roles completed and the final artifact passed.
Only two children were launched and the run completed within budget; child breadth did not exhaust time or prevent delivery.
The implementation assignment was broad but completed, accepted corrections, rebuilt, and did not leave indispensable work unfinished.
The initial brief contained an ordinary incorrect inferred spec, not a requirement already known to the parent at delegation time; verifier feedback corrected it before closure.
Implementation and verification were distinct stages rather than separately implemented components needing a shared API contract; no incompatible interface was produced.
The verifier's concrete findings on length limits and raw argv reached the parent and were passed to the implementer without loss.
Child reports were long enough to be informative but remained decision-structured and were consumed by the parent in subsequent actions.
The parent requested a post-fix verifier rerun against the rebuilt binary, so it did not act on a superseded implementation state.
No incompatible child reports remained unresolved; the initial verifier mismatch report was adjudicated by applying fixes and rerunning tests.
The parent closed after a post-fix full verifier rerun and its own quick sanity check; no visible unresolved integrated gap remained.
The resumed implementation child received concrete checkpointed findings and exact fixes; it was not an unchanged retry that repeated prior work blindly.

candidates.reason: No child was cancelled, stopped, or interrupted before producing needed work; both child trajectories completed.
A complete candidate was built and verified before the final response; no promotable artifact missed the closure window.
The corrective implementation change was followed by a full verifier rerun, so no post-verification merge went unchecked.
The implementation child wrote the final /output project, the parent inspected the tree, and the artifact was evaluated; no completed implementation was left unjoined.
The verifier returned both the initial mismatch report and the final all-match report to the parent before closure.
The initial verifier failure was handled by the parent through a targeted implementation resume and a verifier rerun.
The parent used the verifier's completed mismatch result to request fixes and used the final verifier success result before reporting.
The parent did not wait blindly to a deadline; it inspected child outputs, resumed work, and completed without timeout.
No competing implementations in different files claimed overlapping behavior; verifier was read-only and implementation ownership stayed with agent-0.
Only the implementation child edited source files, so there was no live same-file editing or reconciliation between agents.
The same implementation owner rewrote modules during the fix; no agent replaced source produced or owned by another actor.
Agent-0 owned test11.rs and rebuilds; the verifier only executed binaries, so no other actor overwrote the deliverable.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another agent's final-tree work; Cargo build outputs came from the implementation flow.
Although /output was shared, there was a single implementation writer and no observed unstable-state or provenance problem.
The verifier intentionally consumed the implementer's built binary as the object under test; no unintended generated artifact contaminated reasoning or verification.
